records.source: הָעִ֣זוּ׀בְּנֵ֣י בִניָמִ֗ןמִקֶּ֨רֶב֙ יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם וּבִתְק֨וֹעַ֙ תִּקְע֣וּ שׁוֹפָ֔ר וְעַל־בֵּ֥ית הַכֶּ֖רֶם שְׂא֣וּ מַשְׂאֵ֑ת כִּ֥י רָעָ֛ה נִשְׁקְפָ֥ה מִצָּפ֖וֹן וְשֶׁ֥בֶר גָּדֽוֹל׃
records.gloss: Flee for safety, sons of Benjamin, from [the] midst of Jerusalem, and in Tekoa blow [the] trumpet, and over Beth-haccherem raise [a] signal, for evil looks down from [the] north, and destruction great.
pieces: Run for safety, people of Benjamin, out from the middle of Jerusalem! \q Sound the ram's horn in Tekoa, \q lift up a signal fire over Beth-haccherem! \q For disaster is looming out of the north, a great collapse.

L.1: Flee for safety, sons of Benjamin, from the midst of Jerusalem! \q In Tekoa blow the trumpet, \q and over Beth-haccherem raise a signal! \q For disaster looks down from the north, and great destruction.

R.1: People of Benjamin, run away from Jerusalem to be safe! \q Blow the trumpet in the town of Tekoa. \q Light a fire on the hill of Beth-haccherem to warn people. \q Disaster is about to come from the north. Everything will be crushed.

decisions.choice: Benjamin, Tekoa, Beth-haccherem: places around Jerusalem, named in the order of flight from an enemy coming from the north
decisions.reason: Jerusalem lay on the border of Benjamin, Jeremiah's own tribe (his town, Anathoth, was in Benjamin, 1:1), and many of its people were of Benjamin. Tekoa was a town in the hills about ten miles south of Jerusalem, Amos's home (Amos 1:1). Beth-haccherem was also south of the city (Nehemiah 3:14), probably on a hill where a signal could be seen. People fleeing an army from the north would run south, through these places.

decisions.choice: wordplays on the names: in Tekoa (tiqo'a) blow (tiq'u); Beth-haccherem, 'house of the vineyard'
decisions.reason: The verb "blow" sounds like the name Tekoa, so the alarm is sounded in the town whose name echoes it. Beth-haccherem means "house of the vineyard", which may look ahead to the gleaning of the vine in verse 9. The wordplay cannot be carried over, but the names are kept.

decisions.choice: trumpet ... signal: alarms of war; the signal was probably a fire or smoke signal
decisions.reason: The trumpet was a ram's horn, blown to warn of an attack (Amos 3:6; Hosea 5:8). The word for "signal" comes from the verb "lift up" and was used for a beacon of fire or smoke sent from hill to hill (Judges 20:38, 40).

decisions.choice: disaster looks down from the north: the coming invasion, pictured as looming over the land
decisions.reason: The verb means to look down from a height (Genesis 18:16; Psalm 14:2). The disaster from the north, announced at Jeremiah's call (1:13-15) and in 4:6, is an invading army. The last words, "and great destruction", stand on their own in the Hebrew, as a cry (as 4:6).

decisions.choice: ram's horn ... signal fire
decisions.reason: Balanced follows the settled wording for the trumpet (ram's horn) and says what kind of signal was meant (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: the town of Tekoa ... light a fire on the hill ... to warn people
decisions.reason: Readable explains that Tekoa is a town and what the signal was for, and puts "great destruction" as a full sentence.

records.heading: Flee from Jerusalem

records.source: הַנָּוָה֙ וְהַמְּעֻנָּגָ֔ה דָּמִ֖יתִי בַּת־צִיּֽוֹן׃
records.gloss: The lovely and the delicate I will destroy, [the] daughter of Zion.
pieces: The lovely and pampered one, \q Daughter Zion, I will destroy.

L.2: The lovely and the delicate one \q I will destroy, the daughter of Zion.

R.2: The people of Zion are like a lovely, well-cared-for woman. \q But I will destroy them.

decisions.choice: I will destroy
alternatives: I have likened Daughter Zion to a lovely and delicate one
I have likened Daughter Zion to a lovely pasture
decisions.reason: The verb can come from a root meaning "cut off, destroy" (as Hosea 4:5) or from one meaning "be like, compare". Read as "destroy", God speaks of the coming ruin of the city. Read as "compare", the verse says "I have likened Daughter Zion to a lovely pasture", taking the first word as "pasture" (it has that sense in 23:3; 25:30) and leading into the shepherds and flocks of verse 3. The Hebrew allows both; the sense of judgment is the same either way.

decisions.choice: lovely and delicate: beautiful and used to comfort
decisions.reason: The second word describes someone raised in ease and luxury (Deuteronomy 28:56; Isaiah 47:1). Zion is pictured as a fine, sheltered woman, about to be overrun.

decisions.choice: daughter of Zion: Jerusalem and its people, pictured as a young woman
decisions.reason: As in Isaiah 1:8, "daughter" personifies the city and its people as a woman under God's care.

decisions.choice: the people of Zion are like a lovely, well-cared-for woman
decisions.reason: Readable says "the people of Zion", as the settled wording for this phrase, and makes the picture of a woman explicit.

records.source: אֵלֶ֛יהָ יָבֹ֥אוּ רֹעִ֖ים וְעֶדְרֵיהֶ֑ם תָּקְע֨וּ עָלֶ֤יהָ אֹהָלִים֙ סָבִ֔יב רָע֖וּ אִ֥ישׁ אֶת־יָדֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: To her will come shepherds and their flocks; they will pitch against her tents all around; they will graze each [his] hand.
pieces: Shepherds will come against her with their flocks; \q they will set up tents on every side of her, \q and each will graze his own patch.

L.3: To her shepherds will come with their flocks; \q they will pitch tents against her all around; \q they will graze, each [in] his place.

R.3: Enemy kings will come against her with their armies, like shepherds with their flocks. \q They will set up their tents all around her. \q Each one will take the part he wants.

decisions.choice: shepherds with their flocks: foreign rulers with their armies
decisions.reason: Kings and leaders are often called shepherds (2:8; 12:10; 25:34). Here enemy commanders come with their troops and camp around Jerusalem, and the flocks strip the land bare as an army does when it lays siege.

decisions.choice: hand: portion, the place each one takes
decisions.reason: "Hand" can mean a share or a space beside something (Numbers 2:17; Deuteronomy 23:13). Each commander takes his own part of the land around the city.

decisions.choice: enemy kings ... with their armies, like shepherds with their flocks
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture (meaning decision m1) and keeps the shepherds as a comparison.

records.source: קַדְּשׁ֤וּ עָלֶ֨יהָ֙ מִלְחָמָ֔ה ק֖וּמוּ וְנַעֲלֶ֣ה בַֽצָּהֳרָ֑יִם א֥וֹי לָ֨נוּ֙ כִּי־פָנָ֣ה הַיּ֔וֹם כִּ֥י יִנָּט֖וּ צִלְלֵי־עָֽרֶב׃
records.gloss: Consecrate against her war; arise and let us go up at noon. Woe to us, for has turned the day, for are stretched out [the] shadows of evening.
pieces: "Make ready a holy war against her! \q Up, let us attack at noon!" \q "Woe to us! The day is fading, \q and the evening shadows are growing long!

L.4: "Consecrate war against her! \q Arise, and let us go up at noon!" \q "Woe to us, for the day has turned, \q for the shadows of evening are stretched out!

R.4: The enemy says, "Get ready for battle against her! \q Come on! Let us attack at noon!" \q "How terrible this is for us! The day is almost over. \q The evening shadows are getting long.

decisions.choice: the attackers speak (verses 4-5)
decisions.reason: The commands and the cry "woe to us" are the voice of the enemy army, urging one another on. They want to attack at midday, and when the day runs out they resolve to attack at night (verse 5). The words are quoted as their speech.

decisions.choice: consecrate war: prepare for battle with religious rites
decisions.reason: Armies offered sacrifices and kept rules of purity before going into battle (1 Samuel 7:9; 13:9-12; Joel 4:9). The enemy treats its attack as a holy act; the reader knows that it is God who is sending it (verse 6).

decisions.choice: woe to us, the day has turned: the attackers' frustration that daylight is running out
decisions.reason: Noon was not a usual time to attack, since it was the heat of the day (2 Samuel 4:5). The attackers are so eager that they plan an assault then, and complain as the afternoon wears on.

decisions.choice: Woe to us (Balanced); How terrible this is for us (Readable)
decisions.reason: This is the book-wide wording for a cry of "woe" said of oneself, as in 4:13 and Isaiah. Here the attackers cry it, frustrated that the daylight is running out (m3).

decisions.choice: the enemy says
decisions.reason: Readable names the speaker (meaning decision m1).

records.source: ק֚וּמוּ וְנַעֲלֶ֣ה בַלָּ֔יְלָה וְנַשְׁחִ֖יתָה אַרְמְנוֹתֶֽיהָ׃ס
records.gloss: Arise, and let us go up by night, and let us destroy her fortresses.
pieces: Up, let us attack by night \q and destroy her strongholds!"

L.5: Arise, and let us go up by night, \q and let us destroy her fortresses!"

R.5: Come on! Let us attack at night \q and destroy her strong buildings!"

decisions.choice: fortresses: the fortified buildings of the city
decisions.reason: The word means the strong, high buildings of a city, palaces and towers, the places the rich and powerful lived (17:27; Amos 1:4; Psalm 48:4).

decisions.choice: up, let us attack / come on, let us attack
decisions.reason: "Go up" is the usual verb for marching against a city. Balanced and Readable say "attack", as in verse 4.

records.source: כִּ֣י כֹ֤ה אָמַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת כִּרְת֣וּ עֵצָ֔ה וְשִׁפְכ֥וּ עַל־יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם סֹלְלָ֑ה הִ֚יא הָעִ֣יר הָפְקַ֔ד כֻּלָּ֖הּ עֹ֥שֶׁק בְּקִרְבָּֽהּ׃
records.gloss: For thus says Yahweh of hosts: cut down her trees and pour out against Jerusalem a siege mound. She [is] the city to be punished; all of her [is] oppression in her midst.
pieces: For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies says this: \q Cut down her trees \q and heap up a siege ramp against Jerusalem. \q This is the city marked for punishment; \q inside her is oppression and nothing else.

L.6: For thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts: \q Cut down her trees, \q and pour out a siege mound against Jerusalem. \q This is the city to be punished; \q she is all oppression within.

R.6: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies says: \q Cut down the trees around Jerusalem. \q Pile up dirt to make a ramp against her walls. \q This city must be punished, \q because inside her people are treated cruelly everywhere.

decisions.choice: the LORD gives the orders to the enemy
decisions.reason: The commands to cut trees and build a siege ramp are spoken by God himself. The attackers think they are fighting their own war (verses 4-5); in truth God has summoned them to punish his city (1:15).

decisions.choice: siege mound: a ramp of earth and timber built up to the wall
decisions.reason: Besieging armies cut trees for ramps, towers and battering rams, and heaped earth into a ramp so that siege engines could reach the top of the wall (2 Samuel 20:15; 2 Kings 19:32; Ezekiel 4:2). The law forbade Israel itself to cut down fruit trees in a siege (Deuteronomy 20:19-20).

decisions.choice: the city to be punished: the city God has called to account
decisions.reason: The verb means "to visit" in the sense of calling someone to account (as verse 15). The form is unusual; the Greek translation reads it as "city of falsehood". The sense of the Hebrew as it stands is that this is the city marked out for judgment.

decisions.choice: all of her is oppression: oppression fills the city
decisions.reason: Oppression is the abuse of the weak by the strong, cheating them and taking what is theirs (7:6; 22:17). The Hebrew compresses it: the whole city is oppression.

decisions.choice: pile up dirt to make a ramp against her walls ... because ... people are treated cruelly
decisions.reason: Readable explains what a siege ramp was and says what oppression means, and adds "because" to join the two lines, which the context implies.

records.source: כְּהָקִ֥יר בַּ֨יִר֙ מֵימֶ֔יהָ כֵּ֖ן הֵקֵ֣רָה רָעָתָ֑הּ חָמָ֣ס וָ֠שֹׁד יִשָּׁ֨מַע בָּ֧הּ עַל־פָּנַ֛י תָּמִ֖יד חֳלִ֥י וּמַכָּֽה׃
records.gloss: As keeps fresh a well its waters, so she keeps fresh her evil; violence and destruction is heard in her; before my face continually [are] sickness and wound.
pieces: As a well keeps its water fresh, \q so she keeps her wickedness flowing. \q Violence and ruin echo in her streets; sickness and wounds are always before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

L.7: As a well keeps its waters fresh, \q so she keeps her evil fresh; \q violence and destruction are heard in her; before {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} face continually are sickness and wounds.

R.7: A well always has fresh water coming into it. \q In the same way, Jerusalem always has new evil coming out of her. \q People there cry out, "Violence! Destruction!" I always see her people sick and wounded.

decisions.choice: a well
decisions.reason: The written text and the reading the scribes marked for reading aloud differ in spelling between two forms of the word for a cistern or well. The reading aloud is followed; both mean a source of water.

decisions.choice: keeps fresh: keeps water cool and flowing
decisions.reason: The verb is used only here. It seems to mean to keep water cool and fresh, as a spring-fed well does. Jerusalem's evil never goes stale; it is always new, as if from a spring.

decisions.choice: violence and destruction are heard in her: the cry of people who are wronged
decisions.reason: "Violence and destruction" was the cry of victims calling for help (20:8; Habakkuk 1:2-3). The city is full of the sounds of oppression.

decisions.choice: sickness and wounds before my face: God sees the harm done to the people
decisions.reason: The sickness and wounds are the injuries the powerful inflict on the weak, and the wounds the people bring on themselves by their sin (verse 14; 10:19). God sees them always.

decisions.choice: new evil coming out of her ... people there cry out, "Violence! Destruction!"
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the comparison, names Jerusalem, and puts the sounds heard in the city as the cry of the people (meaning decision m3).

records.source: הִוָּסְרִי֙ יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם פֶּן־תֵּקַ֥ע נַפְשִׁ֖י מִמֵּ֑ךְ פֶּן־אֲשִׂימֵ֣ךְ שְׁמָמָ֔ה אֶ֖רֶץ ל֥וֹא נוֹשָֽׁבָה׃פ
records.gloss: Be warned, Jerusalem, lest be torn my soul from you, lest I make you a desolation, a land not inhabited.
pieces: Take correction, Jerusalem, \q or I will turn from you in disgust, \q and make you a wasteland, \q a land where no one lives.

L.8: Be warned, Jerusalem, \q lest {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} soul be torn away from you, \q lest I make you a desolation, \q a land not inhabited.

R.8: People of Jerusalem, listen to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} warning! \q If you do not, I will turn away from you. \q I will make your land empty, \q and no one will live there.

decisions.choice: be warned: accept discipline and correction
decisions.reason: The verb means to let oneself be taught or corrected, as a child by a parent (2:30; 31:18). It is a last appeal before judgment.

decisions.choice: lest my soul be torn from you: lest God turn away from Jerusalem in revulsion
decisions.reason: "Soul" here is God's very self. The verb means to be wrenched or pulled away (Ezekiel 23:17-18, of turning away in disgust). God warns that his patience with the city may break and he may turn from it altogether.

decisions.choice: turn from you in disgust / turn away from you
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the picture of the soul being torn away as God turning away, which is its meaning (meaning decision m2).

records.source: כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ יְהֹוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת עוֹלֵ֛ל יְעוֹלְל֥וּ כַגֶּ֖פֶן שְׁאֵרִ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל הָשֵׁב֙ יָדְךָ֔ כְּבוֹצֵ֖ר עַל־סַלְסִלּֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: Thus says Yahweh of hosts: thoroughly they will glean like a vine [the] remnant of Israel; pass again your hand like a grape-gatherer over [the] branches.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies says this: \q They will glean the remnant of Israel as bare as a vine. \q Reach out your hand again like one picking grapes, \q over the branches.

L.9: Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts: \q They will glean thoroughly, as [from] a vine, the remnant of Israel; \q pass your hand again, like a grape gatherer, over the branches.

R.9: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies says: \q The enemy will pick the people of Israel clean, like grapes left on a vine. \q Go over the branches again, \q like someone picking grapes.

decisions.choice: glean thoroughly: strip the vine of the last grapes left after the harvest
decisions.reason: After the grape harvest the poor were allowed to gather what was left (Leviticus 19:10; Deuteronomy 24:21). Here the gleaners leave nothing. Even the remnant, the few left after earlier invasions, will be taken (compare 49:9).

decisions.choice: pass your hand again: a command to the one doing the gleaning
decisions.reason: The verb is a command to one person. It may be addressed to the enemy, told to go over the vine again, or to the prophet, told to search the people once more for any who are faithful (5:1). The picture of judgment is the same either way.

decisions.choice: the remnant of Israel: the people of Judah who are left
decisions.reason: The northern kingdom had already fallen to Assyria. "Israel" here is the people of God left in Judah.

decisions.choice: the enemy will pick the people of Israel clean
decisions.reason: Readable names the enemy as the ones gleaning and says "the people of Israel" for "the remnant of Israel".

records.source: עַל־מִ֨י אֲדַבְּרָ֤ה וְאָעִ֨ידָה֙ וְיִשְׁמָ֔עוּ הִנֵּה֙ עֲרֵלָ֣ה אָזְנָ֔ם וְלֹ֥א יוּכְל֖וּ לְהַקְשִׁ֑יב הִנֵּ֣ה דְבַר־יְהוָ֗ה הָיָ֥ה לָהֶ֛ם לְחֶרְפָּ֖ה לֹ֥א יַחְפְּצוּ־בֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: To whom will I speak and warn, that they may hear? Look, uncircumcised [is] their ear, and not they are able to pay attention. Look, [the] word of Yahweh has become to them a reproach; not they delight in it.
pieces: Who is there for me to speak to and warn, so that they will listen? \q Their ears are uncircumcised; \q they cannot pay attention. \q The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has become something they mock; they take no pleasure in it.

L.10: To whom shall I speak and give warning, that they may hear? \q Look, their ear is uncircumcised, \q and they are not able to pay attention. \q Look, the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has become to them a reproach; they do not delight in it.

R.10: Is there anyone I can talk to and warn? Will anyone listen? \q Their ears are closed, \q so they cannot hear. \q They laugh at the message from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. They do not want it at all.

decisions.choice: the prophet speaks
decisions.reason: The "I" here is Jeremiah. Sent to warn the people, he asks whether anyone will listen. In verse 11 he says he is full of God's anger, and God answers him.

decisions.choice: their ear is uncircumcised: their ears are closed, unable to receive God's word
decisions.reason: Circumcision was the sign of belonging to God's covenant (Genesis 17:10-11). An uncircumcised ear is one that has not been opened to God, as if covered over, so that his word cannot get in. Jeremiah uses the same picture of the heart (4:4; 9:25), and Stephen joins the two (Acts 7:51).

decisions.choice: a reproach: something scorned and mocked
decisions.reason: The word means disgrace, an object of contempt. The people treat God's word as a joke (20:8).

decisions.choice: uncircumcised
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the picture because Jeremiah uses it of the heart as well (4:4; 9:25) and the New Testament takes it up (Acts 7:51). Readable gives its meaning, "closed".

records.source: וְאֵת֩ חֲמַ֨ת יְהוָ֤ה׀מָלֵ֨אתִי֙ נִלְאֵ֣יתִי הָכִ֔יל שְׁפֹ֤ךְ עַל־עוֹלָל֙ בַּח֔וּץ וְעַ֛ל ס֥וֹד בַּחוּרִ֖ים יַחְדָּ֑ו כִּֽי־גַם־אִ֤ישׁ עִם־אִשָּׁה֙ יִלָּכֵ֔דוּ זָקֵ֖ן עִם־מְלֵ֥א יָמִֽים׃
records.gloss: And [the] wrath of Yahweh I am full [of]; I am weary of holding in. Pour out on [the] child in the street and on [the] gathering of young men together; for also husband with wife will be taken, old with full of days.
pieces: But I am filled with the fury of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; I am worn out from holding it back. \q Pour it out on the little ones in the street \q and on the young men where they gather; \q for husband and wife alike will be captured, \q the elderly and those who have lived out their years.

L.11: But I am full of the wrath of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; I am weary of holding [it] in. \q Pour [it] out on the child in the street, \q and on the gathering of young men together; \q for both husband with wife will be taken, \q the old with the one full of days.

R.11: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s anger fills me. I am tired of keeping it inside. \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says: Pour it out on the children playing in the street \q and on the young men standing together. \q Husbands and wives will be taken away. \q So will old people and those who are very old.

decisions.choice: the prophet speaks first, then God answers
alternatives: I am weary of holding it in, and of pouring it out on the child in the street
decisions.reason: "I am full" and "I am weary" are Jeremiah's words: God's anger at the people burns in him as God's word does (20:9). The command "pour it out" is God's reply, telling the prophet to announce the judgment on everyone. The verb can also be read "to pour it out", continuing the prophet's words ("I am weary of holding it in, of pouring it out"), but the form is a command.

decisions.choice: the wrath of the LORD: God's burning anger at sin
decisions.reason: The word is used of hot anger, like poison or fire (4:4; 7:20). It is God's holy anger against the evil of his people, which the prophet carries as his message.

decisions.choice: child ... young men ... husband and wife ... old ... full of days: every age of life
decisions.reason: The list runs from small children to the very old. "Full of days" means someone who has lived a long life (Genesis 25:8; 35:29). No one in the city will escape.

decisions.choice: the LORD says
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one who gives the command (meaning decision m1), and adds "playing" and "standing" to make the scenes clear.

decisions.choice: captured / taken away
decisions.reason: The verb means to be caught, as in a trap or in war. Balanced and Readable make clear that the people will be taken by the enemy.

records.source: וְנָסַ֤בּוּ בָֽתֵּיהֶם֙ לַאֲחֵרִ֔ים שָׂד֥וֹת וְנָשִׁ֖ים יַחְדָּ֑ו כִּֽי־אַטֶּ֧ה אֶת־יָדִ֛י עַל־יֹשְׁבֵ֥י הָאָ֖רֶץ נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And will be turned over their houses to others, fields and wives together; for I will stretch out my hand against [the] inhabitants of the land, declares Yahweh.
pieces: Their houses will pass to others, \q their fields and their wives too; \q for I will stretch out {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand against the people of the land, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.12: And their houses will be turned over to others, \q fields and wives together; \q for I will stretch out {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand against the inhabitants of the land, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.12: Other people will take their houses, \q their fields and their wives. \q I will use {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} power to punish the people who live in this land, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: houses, fields and wives given to others: the curse for breaking the covenant
decisions.reason: The Law warned that a disobedient people would see their houses, vineyards and wives taken by others (Deuteronomy 28:30). Verses 12-15 are repeated, with small changes, in 8:10-12.

decisions.choice: stretch out my hand against: act in power to strike
decisions.reason: God's outstretched hand brought plagues on Egypt (Exodus 7:5) and is now turned against his own people (21:5; Isaiah 5:25).

decisions.choice: I will use my power to punish
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idiom of the stretched-out hand (meaning decision m2).

records.source: כִּ֤י מִקְּטַנָּם֙ וְעַד־גְּדוֹלָ֔ם כֻּלּ֖וֹ בּוֹצֵ֣עַ בָּ֑צַע וּמִנָּבִיא֙ וְעַד־כֹּהֵ֔ן כֻּלּ֖וֹ עֹ֥שֶׂה שָּֽׁקֶר׃
records.gloss: For from their least and to their greatest, all of him [is] gaining unjust gain; and from prophet and to priest, all of him [is] doing falsehood.
pieces: For from the smallest of them to the greatest, \q all are out for dishonest gain; \q from prophet to priest, \q every one of them deals in lies.

L.13: For from their least and to their greatest, \q every one of them is gaining unjust gain; \q and from prophet and to priest, \q every one of them practices falsehood.

R.13: Everyone wants to get rich by cheating others, \q from the least important person to the most important. \q Even the prophets and the priests \q all tell lies.

decisions.choice: from their least to their greatest: everyone, of every rank
decisions.reason: The pair names the two ends of society, the humble and the powerful, to include everyone between (31:34; 42:1). Even the leaders who should guide the people are corrupt.

decisions.choice: gaining unjust gain: seeking profit by any means
decisions.reason: The noun means profit got by violence or dishonesty (22:17; Ezekiel 22:27). The repeated root stresses greed: everyone grabs what they can.

decisions.choice: practices falsehood: deals deceitfully, and speaks lies
decisions.reason: "Falsehood" covers both dishonest dealing and false words. In Jeremiah the word is used often of prophets who speak lies in God's name (5:31; 14:14; 23:25). The next verse gives an example of their lies.

decisions.choice: verses 13-15 are repeated in 8:10-12
decisions.reason: Jeremiah 8:10-12 repeats these lines almost word for word. The repetition shows that this was a charge the prophet brought more than once.

decisions.choice: all are out for dishonest gain / wants to get rich by cheating others
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the repeated root ("gaining gain") as the greed it describes.

records.source: וַֽיְרַפְּא֞וּ אֶת־שֶׁ֤בֶר עַמִּי֙ עַל־נְקַלָּ֔ה לֵאמֹ֖ר שָׁל֣וֹם׀שָׁל֑וֹם וְאֵ֖ין שָׁלֽוֹם׃
records.gloss: And they have healed [the] fracture of my people lightly, saying, Peace, peace, and there is no peace.
pieces: They have treated the fracture of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people as though it were slight, \q saying, "Peace, peace," \q when there is no peace.

L.14: And they have healed the fracture of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people lightly, \q saying, "Peace, peace," \q and there is no peace.

R.14: My people are badly hurt, but the leaders treat the wound as if it were only a scratch. \q They say, "Peace, peace!" \q But there is no peace.

decisions.choice: the fracture of my people: the nation's deep injury, a broken bone
decisions.reason: The word means a break, a fracture of a bone or a breaking of a nation (4:6; 8:21; 10:19). The people's sin and the disaster coming on them are a deep wound; the prophets and priests of verse 13 treat it as if it were nothing.

decisions.choice: lightly: as a trifling matter
decisions.reason: The form means "something slight". They give the wound a quick, careless dressing, as if it were not serious.

decisions.choice: peace: safety, everything well, no disaster coming
decisions.reason: Peace here is well-being and safety: no war, no judgment. The false prophets promise it in God's name (14:13; 23:17), while God is sending an army from the north. The same words return in 8:11.

decisions.choice: Peace, peace, when there is no peace: repeated in 8:11 and echoed by Ezekiel
decisions.reason: Jeremiah 8:11 repeats this verse, with "the daughter of my people" in place of "my people". Ezekiel brings the same charge against the prophets who say "Peace" when there is none (Ezekiel 13:10, 16).

decisions.choice: my people are badly hurt, but the leaders treat the wound as if it were only a scratch
decisions.reason: Readable names the prophets and priests of verse 13 as "the leaders", and states the people's hurt before the careless healing, so that the comparison is clear.

decisions.choice: peace (not "all is well")
decisions.reason: "Peace" is kept at every level, since it is the word the prophets promised and the saying is repeated in 8:11. The same wording is used there at each level.

records.source: הֹבִ֕ישׁוּ כִּ֥י תוֹעֵבָ֖ה עָשׂ֑וּ גַּם־בּ֣וֹשׁ לֹֽא־יֵב֗וֹשׁוּ גַּם־הַכְלִים֙ לֹ֣א יָדָ֔עוּ לָכֵ֞ן יִפְּל֧וּ בַנֹּפְלִ֛ים בְּעֵת־פְּקַדְתִּ֥ים יִכָּשְׁל֖וּ אָמַ֥ר יְהוָֽה׃ס
records.gloss: Were they ashamed that abomination they have done? Also be ashamed not they are ashamed, also to blush not they know. Therefore they will fall among the falling; at [the] time I visit them they will stumble, says Yahweh.
pieces: Were they ashamed when they did such detestable things? \q Not in the least; they have forgotten how to blush. \q So they will fall with the fallen; \q when I call them to account they will be brought down, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.15: Were they ashamed when they did abomination? \q No, they were not at all ashamed, and they did not know how to blush. \q Therefore they will fall among those who fall; \q at the time I punish them they will stumble, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.15: They have done disgusting things. Do they feel ashamed? \q No, not at all! They have not even learned how to blush. \q That is why they will die with all the others who die. \q When I punish them, they will fall, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: were they ashamed? a question with no question marker
alternatives: They acted shamefully when they did abomination
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has no word marking a question, but the next lines answer it: they felt no shame at all. The verb could also be read as a statement, "they acted shamefully when they did abomination". 8:12 has the same words.

decisions.choice: abomination: what God finds detestable
decisions.reason: The word is used of idolatry and of grave wrongs that God hates (2:7; 7:10; Deuteronomy 18:9-12).

decisions.choice: the time I visit them: the time of punishment
decisions.reason: God's "visiting" is his coming to call to account (as verse 6). For a guilty people it means judgment (8:12; 10:15).

decisions.choice: they will die with all the others who die
decisions.reason: "Fall among the fallen" means to be killed in battle with the rest. Readable says so.

records.source: כֹּ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֡ה עִמְדוּ֩ עַל־דְּרָכִ֨ים וּרְא֜וּ וְשַׁאֲל֣וּ׀לִנְתִב֣וֹת עוֹלָ֗ם אֵי־זֶ֨ה דֶ֤רֶךְ הַטּוֹב֙ וּלְכוּ־בָ֔הּ וּמִצְא֥וּ מַרְגּ֖וֹעַ לְנַפְשְׁכֶ֑ם וַיֹּאמְר֖וּ לֹ֥א נֵלֵֽךְ׃
records.gloss: Thus says Yahweh: stand at [the] roads and look, and ask for paths of long ago, where this [is] the way the good, and walk in it, and find rest for your souls. And they said, Not we will walk.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says this: Stand where the roads meet and look around; ask about the age-old paths, which one is the good way, \q and walk in it; then you will find rest for your souls. \q But they answered, "We will not go that way."

L.16: Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: Stand at the roads and look, and ask for the paths of long ago, which [is] the good way; \q and walk in it, and find rest for your souls. \q But they said, "We will not walk [in it]."

R.16: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: \q Stand where the roads cross, and look. Ask about the old paths your people walked long ago. Ask which way is good. Then walk in it. There you will find rest for your souls. \q But they answered, "We will not walk in it."

decisions.choice: roads, ancient paths, the good way: the way of life God had shown his people from the beginning
decisions.reason: The people stand like travelers at a crossroads, choosing which way to go. The "paths of long ago" are the ways of the covenant, the life of faithfulness that God taught Israel in the past (18:15; Deuteronomy 32:7). The good way is the one that leads to life (Deuteronomy 30:15-16).

decisions.choice: rest for your souls: rest and well-being for your whole self
decisions.reason: "Soul" means the whole person, the living self. The rest is the settled peace of those who walk in God's way, the opposite of the restless wandering of 2:23-25.

decisions.choice: find rest for your souls: taken up by Jesus in Matthew 11:29
decisions.reason: Jesus uses these words when he calls the weary to come to him and learn from him: "you will find rest for your souls" (Matthew 11:29).

decisions.choice: rest for your souls
decisions.reason: "Souls" is kept at every level so that the words Jesus quotes in Matthew 11:29 can be recognized.

decisions.choice: the old paths your people walked long ago
decisions.reason: Readable explains that the old paths are the ways the people walked in the past (meaning decision m1).

records.heading: The age-old paths

records.source: וַהֲקִמֹתִ֤י עֲלֵיכֶם֙ צֹפִ֔ים הַקְשִׁ֖יבוּ לְק֣וֹל שׁוֹפָ֑ר וַיֹּאמְר֖וּ לֹ֥א נַקְשִֽׁיב׃
records.gloss: And I raised up over you watchmen: pay attention to [the] sound of [the] trumpet. And they said, Not we will pay attention.
pieces: I set watchmen over you: \q "Listen for the blast of the ram's horn!" \q But they said, "We will not listen."

L.17: And I raised up watchmen over you: \q "Pay attention to the sound of the trumpet!" \q But they said, "We will not pay attention."

R.17: I gave you watchmen to warn you. \q They said, "Listen for the sound of the trumpet!" \q But the people said, "We will not listen."

decisions.choice: watchmen: the prophets, set to warn the people
decisions.reason: A watchman stood on the city wall and blew the trumpet when he saw an enemy coming (Ezekiel 33:2-6). God gave his people prophets to warn them of judgment in the same way (Ezekiel 3:17; Hosea 9:8).

decisions.choice: pay attention to the trumpet: the watchmen's warning, quoted without a verb of speaking
decisions.reason: The Hebrew moves straight from "I raised up watchmen" to the words they cried. The trumpet is the alarm of verse 1.

decisions.choice: to warn you ... they said ... the people said
decisions.reason: Readable says what the watchmen were for, adds "they said" before their words, and names the people as the ones who refused.

records.source: לָכֵ֖ן שִׁמְע֣וּ הַגּוֹיִ֑ם וּדְעִ֥י עֵדָ֖ה אֶת־אֲשֶׁר־בָּֽם׃
records.gloss: Therefore hear, the nations, and know, congregation, what [is] in them.
pieces: Therefore listen, you nations; \q know, you assembly, what will happen to them.

L.18: Therefore hear, you nations, \q and know, congregation, what [is] against them.

R.18: So listen, all you nations. \q You who are gathered here, learn what will happen to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people.

decisions.choice: congregation, know what is against them: the gathered witnesses are to learn what will come on Judah
alternatives: know, O congregation, what is in them (their sin)
decisions.reason: The line is hard. "Congregation" may be the assembly of the nations, called with the earth (verse 19) as witnesses to God's case against his people; "what is in them" may mean what will happen to them, or what is in the hearts of the people (their guilt). The Greek translation has a different text here ("and those who shepherd their flocks"). The general sense, that the world is called to witness Judah's judgment, is clear.

decisions.choice: my people
decisions.reason: Readable names "them" as God's people, whose judgment is announced in verse 19.

records.source: שִׁמְעִ֣י הָאָ֔רֶץ הִנֵּ֨ה אָנֹכִ֜י מֵבִ֥יא רָעָ֛ה אֶל־הָעָ֥ם הַזֶּ֖ה פְּרִ֣י מַחְשְׁבוֹתָ֑ם כִּ֤י עַל־דְּבָרַי֙ לֹ֣א הִקְשִׁ֔יבוּ וְתוֹרָתִ֖י וַיִּמְאֲסוּ־בָֽהּ׃
records.gloss: Hear, the earth: look, I [am] bringing evil to the people the this, [the] fruit of their schemes; for to my words not they paid attention, and my instruction, and they rejected it.
pieces: Listen, earth! \q I am about to bring disaster on this people, the fruit of their own plotting, \q because they have paid no heed to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} words, \q and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} instruction they have tossed aside.

L.19: Hear, earth: \q Look, I am bringing disaster on this people, the fruit of their schemes, \q for they have not paid attention to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} words, \q and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} instruction, they have rejected it.

R.19: Earth, listen! \q I am going to bring disaster on these people. It is what their evil plans deserve. \q They have not listened to what I said. \q They have turned away from {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} teaching.

decisions.choice: hear, earth: the earth called as witness
decisions.reason: As in Isaiah 1:2 and Deuteronomy 32:1, heaven and earth or the nations are called to witness the case God brings against his people (2:12).

decisions.choice: the fruit of their schemes: the harvest of their own plans
decisions.reason: Their disaster is the crop that grows from what they themselves have planned (17:10; 21:14; Proverbs 1:31). Judgment is what their own deeds produce.

decisions.choice: instruction: God's teaching, his law
decisions.reason: The word is God's teaching, given in the Law, by which his people were to live (2:8; 9:12).

decisions.choice: it is what their evil plans deserve
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of fruit (meaning decision m2).

records.source: לָמָּה־זֶּ֨ה לִ֤י לְבוֹנָה֙ מִשְּׁבָ֣א תָב֔וֹא וְקָנֶ֥ה הַטּ֖וֹב מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מֶרְחָ֑ק עֹלֽוֹתֵיכֶם֙ לֹ֣א לְרָצ֔וֹן וְזִבְחֵיכֶ֖ם לֹא־עָ֥רְבוּ לִֽי׃ס
records.gloss: Why this to me, frankincense from Sheba comes, and the cane the good from a land of distance? Your burnt offerings [are] not for acceptance, and your sacrifices not they are pleasing to me.
pieces: What do I care for incense brought from Sheba, \q or for fragrant cane from a faraway land? \q Your burnt offerings do not win {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} favor; \q your sacrifices give {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} no pleasure.

L.20: Why does it [matter] to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, frankincense that comes from Sheba, \q and the sweet cane from a distant land? \q Your burnt offerings are not acceptable, \q and your sacrifices are not pleasing to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

R.20: You bring {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} expensive incense from the land of Sheba. \q You bring sweet-smelling cane from a land far away. But why should I care about that? \q I will not accept your burnt offerings. \q Your sacrifices do not please {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

decisions.choice: frankincense from Sheba, sweet cane: costly imported spices used in worship
decisions.reason: Frankincense was a fragrant resin burned as incense (Leviticus 2:1-2). Sheba, in the south of Arabia, was famous for it and for spices (1 Kings 10:1-2; Isaiah 60:6). Sweet cane was a fragrant reed used in the holy anointing oil (Exodus 30:23). These were rich, rare offerings brought from far away.

decisions.choice: offerings not accepted: worship without obedience does not please God
decisions.reason: God does not reject sacrifice as such. He rejects the offerings of people who will not listen to his words (verse 19). The prophets bring the same charge again and again (7:21-23; Isaiah 1:11-15; Amos 5:21-24; 1 Samuel 15:22).

decisions.choice: incense
decisions.reason: Balanced says "incense", which names what frankincense was used for; Literal keeps "frankincense".

decisions.choice: you bring ... But why should I care about that?
decisions.reason: Readable states what the people bring first and then gives God's question, so that the question is easy to follow.

records.source: לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה הִנְנִ֥י נֹתֵ֛ן אֶל־הָעָ֥ם הַזֶּ֖ה מִכְשֹׁלִ֑ים וְכָ֣שְׁלוּ בָ֠ם אָב֨וֹת וּבָנִ֥ים יַחְדָּ֛ו שָׁכֵ֥ן וְרֵע֖וֹ וְאָבָֽדוּ׃פ
records.gloss: Therefore thus says Yahweh: look, I [am] putting to the people the this stumbling blocks, and they will stumble against them, fathers and sons together; neighbor and his friend, and they will perish.
pieces: So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says this: \q I am about to set obstacles in front of this people, \q and they will trip over them, parents and children alike; neighbors and friends will die.

L.21: Therefore thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: \q Look, I am putting stumbling blocks before this people, \q and they will stumble over them, fathers and sons together; neighbor and his friend will perish.

R.21: So this is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: \q I will put things in the way of these people to make them fall. \q Parents and children will trip over them. Neighbors and friends will die.

decisions.choice: I am putting stumbling blocks: God himself brings about the fall the people have chosen
decisions.reason: The stumbling blocks are the disasters God sends in judgment (Ezekiel 3:20). They are not traps for the innocent: the people have refused the good way (verse 16), and now the road they chose will bring them down (Isaiah 8:14-15).

decisions.choice: and they will perish
decisions.reason: The written text has "they will perish" without "and"; the reading the scribes marked for reading aloud adds "and". The meaning is the same. The reading aloud is followed.

decisions.choice: fathers and sons, neighbor and friend: everyone, family and community
decisions.reason: The pairs take in every generation and every relationship (13:14). No one will be spared.

decisions.choice: parents and children
decisions.reason: "Fathers and sons" means the generations of a family, not men only, so Balanced and Readable say "parents and children"; Literal keeps the Hebrew words.

records.source: כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה הִנֵּ֛ה עַ֥ם בָּ֖א מֵאֶ֣רֶץ צָפ֑וֹן וְג֣וֹי גָּד֔וֹל יֵע֖וֹר מִיַּרְכְּתֵי־אָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: Thus says Yahweh: look, a people coming from a land of [the] north, and a nation great will be stirred up from [the] remotest parts of [the] earth.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says this: \q See, an army is coming from the land of the north; \q a mighty nation is being roused from the ends of the earth.

L.22: Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: \q Look, a people is coming from the land of the north, \q and a great nation will be stirred up from the farthest parts of the earth.

R.22: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: \q Look! An army is coming from the land in the north. \q A powerful nation is getting ready to fight. It is coming from far away.

decisions.choice: a people from the land of the north: the Babylonian army
decisions.reason: Babylon lay to the east, but armies from it came into Judah from the north, along the road through Syria. The enemy from the north, first announced in 1:14-15 and named in 25:9, is Babylon under Nebuchadnezzar.

decisions.choice: turned against Babylon in 50:41-43
decisions.reason: These lines (verses 22-24) are repeated almost word for word in 50:41-43, where they are spoken against Babylon itself: the nation that came from the north will in turn face an enemy from the north.

decisions.choice: the farthest parts of the earth: distant lands, the far edges of the known world
decisions.reason: The phrase means a place very far off (25:32; 31:8). The enemy is strange and distant, beyond Israel's horizon.

decisions.choice: an army
decisions.reason: The word is "a people", but here it means a people on the march for war, so Balanced and Readable say "an army".

records.heading: An army from the land of the north

records.source: קֶ֣שֶׁת וְכִיד֞וֹן יַחֲזִ֗יקוּ אַכְזָרִ֥י הוּא֙ וְלֹ֣א יְרַחֵ֔מוּ קוֹלָם֙ כַּיָּ֣ם יֶהֱמֶ֔ה וְעַל־סוּסִ֖ים יִרְכָּ֑בוּ עָר֗וּךְ כְּאִישׁ֙ לַמִּלְחָמָ֔ה עָלַ֖יִךְ בַּת־צִיּֽוֹן׃
records.gloss: Bow and javelin they grasp; cruel [is] it, and not they have mercy; their sound like the sea roars, and on horses they ride, arrayed like a man for battle against you, daughter of Zion.
pieces: They take hold of bow and spear; \q they are cruel and show no mercy. \q The noise of them roars like the sea \q as they ride on horses, \q lined up like a warrior for battle against you, Daughter Zion.

L.23: They grasp bow and javelin; \q it is cruel, and they have no mercy; \q their sound roars like the sea, \q and they ride on horses, \q arrayed like a man for battle against you, daughter of Zion.

R.23: Its soldiers carry bows and spears. \q They are cruel and do not show mercy. \q They ride horses, and they sound like the roaring sea. \q They are lined up, ready to fight against you, people of Zion.

decisions.choice: bow and javelin: the weapons of an army that fights at a distance and up close
decisions.reason: The bow shot from a distance, and the javelin, a short spear, was thrown or used hand to hand (1 Samuel 17:6, 45). Babylon's army was famous for its archers and its horses (4:13, 29).

decisions.choice: it is cruel, and they show no mercy: the nation as one, then its soldiers
decisions.reason: The Hebrew changes from "it" (the nation of verse 22) to "they" (its soldiers). Both mean the same army.

decisions.choice: arrayed like a man for battle: drawn up as one warrior
decisions.reason: The whole army stands in its ranks as if it were one man ready to fight (Joel 2:5).

decisions.choice: spear
decisions.reason: The javelin was a short throwing spear; Balanced and Readable use the more familiar word.

decisions.choice: people of Zion
decisions.reason: Readable says "people of Zion" for "daughter of Zion", as elsewhere.

records.source: שָׁמַ֥עְנוּ אֶת־שָׁמְע֖וֹ רָפ֣וּ יָדֵ֑ינוּ צָרָה֙ הֶחֱזִיקַ֔תְנוּ חִ֖יל כַּיּוֹלֵדָֽה׃
records.gloss: We have heard its report; dropped our hands; distress has seized us, anguish like [a woman] giving birth.
pieces: We have heard the news of them, and our hands hang limp; \q distress has gripped us, \q pain like a woman in labor.

L.24: We have heard the report of it; our hands have dropped; \q distress has seized us, \q anguish like [a woman] giving birth.

R.24: We have heard about this army. We have no strength left. \q We are terrified. \q We hurt like a woman giving birth to a baby.

decisions.choice: we: the people of Jerusalem speak
decisions.reason: The voice changes. Without any word of introduction, the people of the city answer the news of the army, and the prophet speaks with them ("on us", verse 26).

decisions.choice: our hands have dropped: all strength and courage are gone
decisions.reason: Hands that hang down are a picture of helpless fear (2 Samuel 4:1; Isaiah 13:7).

decisions.choice: anguish like a woman giving birth: sudden, overwhelming pain that cannot be escaped
decisions.reason: The prophets compare the terror of war to the pains of childbirth (4:31; 13:21; 22:23; Isaiah 13:8).

decisions.choice: we have no strength left ... we are terrified
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of the hands and names the distress as fear.

records.source: אַל־תֵּֽצְאוּ֙ הַשָּׂדֶ֔ה וּבַדֶּ֖רֶךְ אַל־תֵּלֵ֑כוּ כִּ֚י חֶ֣רֶב לְאֹיֵ֔ב מָג֖וֹר מִסָּבִֽיב׃
records.gloss: Do not go out [to] the field, and on [the] road do not walk; for [a] sword [is] to the enemy, terror from all around.
pieces: Do not go out into the countryside; \q do not travel on the roads; \q for the enemy's sword is there, \q terror on every side.

L.25: Do not go out into the field, \q and do not walk on the road, \q for the enemy has a sword; \q terror is on every side.

R.25: Do not go out into the fields. \q Do not walk on the roads. \q The enemy is there with swords. \q There is terror all around!

decisions.choice: do not go out, do not walk: spoken to many people
decisions.reason: The written text has the two verbs as commands to one woman, the city herself, as in verse 26 ("daughter of my people"); the reading the scribes marked for reading aloud has them as commands to many people. The meaning is the same: no one should leave the city. The reading aloud is followed.

decisions.choice: terror on every side: one of Jeremiah's sayings
decisions.reason: The phrase returns in 20:3, 10; 46:5; 49:29 and Lamentations 2:22 (compare Psalm 31:14). Jeremiah gives it as a name to Pashhur the priest (20:3), and his enemies throw it back at him (20:10).

decisions.choice: field and road: outside the city walls
decisions.reason: When an enemy is in the land, the fields and roads outside the walls are where people are caught and killed (14:18). Only the city gives any shelter.

decisions.choice: terror on every side / terror all around
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the same wording as in 20:3, 10 so the saying can be recognized.

records.source: בַּת־עַמִּ֤י חִגְרִי־שָׂק֙ וְהִתְפַּלְּשִׁ֣י בָאֵ֔פֶר אֵ֤בֶל יָחִיד֙ עֲשִׂ֣י לָ֔ךְ מִסְפַּ֖ד תַּמְרוּרִ֑ים כִּ֣י פִתְאֹ֔ם יָבֹ֥א הַשֹּׁדֵ֖ד עָלֵֽינוּ׃
records.gloss: Daughter of my people, gird on sackcloth and roll in ashes; mourning of an only [son] make for yourself, lamentation of bitterness; for suddenly will come the destroyer upon us.
pieces: My dear people, put on sackcloth \q and roll in the ashes; \q mourn as for an only son, \q with the bitterest wailing; \q for suddenly the destroyer will fall on us.

L.26: Daughter of my people, gird on sackcloth, \q and roll in ashes; \q make for yourself mourning as for an only [son], \q a lament most bitter; \q for suddenly the destroyer will come upon us.

R.26: My people, dress in rough cloth to show your sorrow. \q Roll in the ashes. \q Cry as hard as parents who have lost their only son. \q Weep bitterly. \q The one who destroys will suddenly attack us.

decisions.choice: daughter of my people: the people, spoken of with tender grief
decisions.reason: "Daughter" pictures the people as a beloved young woman (as "daughter of Zion", verse 2). The phrase is Jeremiah's own (4:11; 8:11, 19-23; 14:17) and is always used with grief for the people's suffering.

decisions.choice: sackcloth and ashes: the signs of deep mourning
decisions.reason: Mourners wore a rough cloth of goat's hair and sat or rolled in ashes or dust (4:8; 25:34; Micah 1:10).

decisions.choice: mourning for an only son: the deepest grief
decisions.reason: The loss of an only son meant the loss of a family's future and name, and so was the bitterest grief there could be (Amos 8:10; Zechariah 12:10).

decisions.choice: upon us: the prophet counts himself with the people
decisions.reason: The prophet, who calls the people to mourn, says "us": the judgment he announces will fall on him too.

decisions.choice: my dear people / my people
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable follow the settled wording for "daughter of my people" (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: rough cloth to show your sorrow ... parents who have lost their only son
decisions.reason: Readable explains what sackcloth was and whose grief is meant.

records.source: בָּח֛וֹן נְתַתִּ֥יךָ בְעַמִּ֖י מִבְצָ֑ר וְתֵדַ֕ע וּבָחַנְתָּ֖ אֶת־דַּרְכָּֽם׃
records.gloss: An assayer I have made you among my people, a fortress, and you will know and you will test their way.
pieces: I have made you a tester of metals among {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, strong as a fortress, \q so that you may learn and test their ways.

L.27: An assayer I have made you among {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, a fortress, \q that you may know and test their way.

R.27: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to me: I have made you like someone who tests metals. \q You will test {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people to find out how they live.

decisions.choice: God speaks to Jeremiah
decisions.reason: "You" is the prophet. God gives him a task: to test the people as a worker tests ore to see whether it holds silver. Verses 28-30 give the result.

decisions.choice: assayer: one who tests metal to find its worth
decisions.reason: An assayer heated ore to find out how much pure silver it held. The word and the verb "test" (9:6; Psalm 66:10) come from the same root. The prophet's preaching is the fire that shows what the people are made of.

decisions.choice: a fortress
decisions.reason: The word usually means a fortified city, as in 1:18, where God makes Jeremiah "a fortified city" against the people. It can be read here as the same promise, set beside his work as an assayer. With different vowels the same letters could be read "a refiner", which would fit the picture of testing metal more closely.

decisions.choice: the LORD said to me
decisions.reason: Readable names who is speaking to whom (meaning decision m1). It leaves out "fortress", whose sense here is uncertain (meaning decision m3).

records.source: כֻּלָּם֙ סָרֵ֣י סֽוֹרְרִ֔ים הֹלְכֵ֥י רָכִ֖יל נְחֹ֣שֶׁת וּבַרְזֶ֑ל כֻּלָּ֥ם מַשְׁחִיתִ֖ים הֵֽמָּה׃
records.gloss: All of them [are] rebels of rebels, going about [with] slander, bronze and iron; all of them [are] acting corruptly they.
pieces: They are all hardened rebels, \q going around spreading slander. They are bronze and iron; \q every one of them is corrupt.

L.28: All of them are stubborn rebels, \q going about with slander; bronze and iron, \q all of them act corruptly.

R.28: All of them are very stubborn and turn against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. \q They go around telling lies about others. They are like cheap metals, bronze and iron. \q They all do evil things.

decisions.choice: rebels of rebels: the most stubborn of rebels
decisions.reason: Two words from different roots, both meaning to turn away and resist, are joined: "turners-aside of stubborn ones". The phrase works as a strong superlative: they are rebels through and through (compare 5:23).

decisions.choice: going about with slander: spreading damaging talk
decisions.reason: The phrase is used of a gossip who goes about betraying others (9:3; Leviticus 19:16; Proverbs 11:13).

decisions.choice: bronze and iron: base metals with no silver in them
decisions.reason: In the test of verse 27, the people prove to be only the common metals mixed into the ore, not silver (Ezekiel 22:18). The same metals stand for stubborn hardness (Isaiah 48:4).

decisions.choice: turn against me ... like cheap metals
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one they rebel against, and explains the picture of bronze and iron (meaning decision m3).

records.source: נָחַ֣ר מַפֻּ֔חַ מֵאֵ֖שׁ תַּ֣ם עֹפָ֑רֶת לַשָּׁוְא֙ צָרַ֣ף צָר֔וֹף וְרָעִ֖ים לֹ֥א נִתָּֽקוּ׃
records.gloss: Blows [the] bellows, by fire is consumed lead; in vain one refines [and] refines, and [the] evil [ones] not are separated out.
pieces: The bellows blast away, \q the lead is burned up in the fire, \q but the refining goes on for nothing; \q the wicked are not drawn off.

L.29: The bellows blow fiercely; \q the lead is consumed by the fire; \q in vain one keeps refining, \q and the wicked are not separated out.

R.29: The worker uses the bellows to blow air on the fire and make it very hot. \q The lead burns up in the fire. \q But all the work does no good. \q The evil cannot be separated out.

decisions.choice: refining silver: the lead is used up, but nothing pure is left
decisions.reason: In ancient refining, silver ore was heated with lead in a very hot fire, blown with bellows. The lead melted, drew the other metals and dirt (the dross) into itself, and was absorbed or skimmed off, leaving the pure silver behind. Here the bellows blow and the lead burns away, but no silver separates out: the ore is all dross. The prophet's long work of testing has found no pure metal among the people. The details of the process are known from ancient workshops and from other passages (Ezekiel 22:18-22; Malachi 3:2-3), but how exactly each word fits the steps is not certain.

decisions.choice: the lead is consumed by the fire
decisions.reason: The written text can be read "from their fire, lead"; the reading the scribes marked for reading aloud divides the letters as "by the fire, it is consumed". The reading aloud is followed. Both describe the lead in the refining fire.

decisions.choice: the wicked are not separated out
decisions.reason: The wicked are the dross that should come away from the silver. The people's evil is so mixed through them that it cannot be removed.

decisions.choice: the worker uses the bellows to blow air on the fire and make it very hot
decisions.reason: Readable explains what bellows do.

records.source: כֶּ֣סֶף נִמְאָ֔ס קָרְא֖וּ לָהֶ֑ם כִּֽי־מָאַ֥ס יְהוָ֖ה בָּהֶֽם׃פ
records.gloss: Silver rejected they call them, for has rejected Yahweh them.
pieces: They are called worthless silver, \q because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has thrown them away.

L.30: Rejected silver they call them, \q for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has rejected them.

R.30: People will call them silver that has been thrown away. \q That is because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has rejected them.

decisions.choice: rejected silver ... the LORD has rejected them: a play on one verb
decisions.reason: The same verb, "reject", is used twice. The people are called the silver that was thrown away after testing, and the reason is that God has rejected them, as they rejected his instruction (verse 19). The test has shown that there is nothing of worth to keep (compare Isaiah 1:22).

decisions.choice: they call them: people will call them
decisions.reason: The verb has no stated subject. It means "they will be called": this is the name they will have.

decisions.choice: worthless silver ... thrown them away
decisions.reason: Balanced uses two words for the one Hebrew verb to make the picture clear; Literal and Readable keep "rejected" for God's act so that the link with verse 19 is seen.
